docs.title: Overview
docs.text: vx-components is a simple web component library built using lit.

docs.title: registerSvgLibrary()
docs.text:
Parameter Type Comments name string The name of the SVG library. library Record<string, TemplateResult> The SVG library.

Registers an SVG library. If the library already exists, is is replaced.

docs.title: getSvgLibrary()
docs.text:
Parameter Type Comments name string The name of the SVG library.

Returns the SVG library with the given name.

docs.title: hasSvgLibrary()
docs.text:
Parameter Type Comments name string The name of the SVG library.

Returns true if the library exists in the register.

docs.title: svg()
docs.text:
Parameter Type Comments name string The name of the SVG in the format [library].[name]. Eg.: svg("shapes.circle")

Returns a TemplateResult representing the SVG or nothing if the SVG does not exist.

vx-route
docs.text:
vx-route | VxRoute

A vx-route defines an individual route path. A route must be defined as a direct child of a VxRouter element.

Parsing of the route is done by the path-to-regexp package on npm and any parameters extracted stored in the route's paramters property.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
<vx-route path="/home">
        This is the content of the home page
    </vx-route>
The parameter is saved in the route's parameters property and can be interrogated by child elements. 
    <vx-route path="/products/:id">
        <my-products-page></my-products-page>
    </vx-route>
The subroute flag indicate a routing node. A child <vx-router element would be responsible for processing further path fragments. The child router does not have to be a direct child.

    <vx-route path="/products" subroute>
        <my-products-page></my-products-page>
    </vx-route>
Instead of placing content in the default slot, a component can be named. The component element is created and added to the DOM by the route. When the route is no longer active, the element is removed from the DOM. 
    <vx-route path="/products" component="my-products-page" subroute>
    </vx-route>

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type string Default-

The path for this route relative to any parent routes. See path-to-regexp on npmjs.com for an explanation of the path syntax

docs.title: subroute
docs.text:
Type boolean Defaultfalse

Identifies the route as a subroute.

docs.title: component
docs.text:
Type string Defaultnull

This component will be created and added to the DOM instead of rendering the slotted elements.

docs.title: active
docs.text:
Type boolean Defaultfalse

Indicates this path is active. The attribute is automatically set/reset by the parent vx-router component.

docs.title: customTemplate
docs.text:
Type TemplateResult DefaultTemplateResult | () => TemplateResult

An alternative template to use where using slotted elements is not suitable. The value of this property should be set during a vx-connected or vx-activated event.

docs.title: componentRef
docs.text:
Type HtmlElement Defaultundefined

A reference to the component created when the component attribute was specified

docs.title: parameters
docs.text:
Type object Default{}

The parameters extracted from the URL by the route

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event Description vx-connected Called when the route is connected to the DOM. vx-activate Called when the route is about to be activated. vx-activated Called when the route has been activated. vx-deactivate Called when the route is about to be deactivated. vx-deactivated Called when the route has been deactivated.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Name Description (default) Content to be displayed when the route is active and component property is not set.

docs.title: vx-router
docs.text:
vx-router | VxRouter

A vx-router component manages the application's routing. The current URL is checked against a set of defined routes (vx-route components) in the component's content (default slot).

The routes should be defined in order of specificity, ascending or descending depending on the reversed property.

vx-router components can be nested in the DOM.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
<vx-router>
    <vx-route path="/home">
        This is the content of the home page
    </vx-route>
    <vx-route path="/about">
        This is the content of the about page
    </vx-route>
    <vx-route path="/contact">
        This is the content of the contact page
    </vx-route>
</vx-router>

docs.title: reversed
docs.text:
Type boolean Defaultfalse

Normally routes are matched top to bottom, ordered from the most specific to the least specific. When set to true, the order is reversed.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: (default) vx-route components defining the individual routes.

docs.title: vx-svg
docs.text:
vx-svg | VxSVG

The vx-svg component displays an SVG element from a registered SVG library. See SVG Libraries.

docs.title: Examples
library
docs.text:
Type string Default"default"

The name of the registered library the SVG resides in. See SVG Libraries. Id omitted, the default library is used.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
Type string Default(none)

The name of the SVG to display.

docs.title: button
docs.text:
Type boolean Defaultfalse

If button is set, the vx-svg element will be clickable and raise a click event. The cursor will become a pointer and the element highlighted when the mouse is over the element.

docs.title: SVG Libraries
docs.text:
The svg API provides routines for managing and using SVG libraries. A library is a collection of SVG elements stored as a javascript object. By using libraries, there is no need to deploy separate asset files with your application.

For example:

const shapeIcons: SVGLibrary = {

    "circle" : html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1em" height="1em" fill="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
        <path d="M8 15A7 7 0 1 1 8 1a7 7 0 0 1 0 14m0 1A8 8 0 1 0 8 0a8 8 0 0 0 0 16"/>
    </svg>`,

    "square" : html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1em" height="1em" fill="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
        <path d="M14 1a1 1 0 0 1 1 1v12a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H2a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V2a1 1 0 0 1 1-1zM2 0a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v12a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h12a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V2a2 2 0 0 0-2-2z"/>
    </svg>`,

    "square-fill" : html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1em" height="1em" fill="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
        <path d="M0 2a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h12a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H2a2 2 0 0 1-2-2z"/>
    </svg>`
}

// register the library...
registerSvgLibrary("shapes", shapeIcons);

The shapes can be used via the svg() function or vx-svg component.

svg()vx-svg 
svg("shapes.square");

<vx-svg library="shapes" name="square"></vx-svg>
